name: protocols
description: Every registered answer protocol; in_crossing marks the five of the format by protocol experiment.

python_call.name: Python-style function call
python_call.description: Answer with `tool_name(arg=value)`. Keyword arguments carry the names, so no JSON structure is needed.

python_list_call.name: Bracketed list of Python calls
python_list_call.description: `[f(a=1), g(b=2)]`: Llama 3.1's parallel-call shape, where several calls are one bracketed list.

bfcl_python_list.name: BFCL's bracketed Python call list, BFCL's words
bfcl_python_list.description: `[func_name1(params_name1=params_value1, ...), func_name2(params)]`, asked for in the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard's own sentence.

cli_call.name: Command-line invocation
cli_call.description: `tool_name --arg value --flag`. Values are untyped text, so the schema has to supply the types.

graphql_call.name: GraphQL mutation
graphql_call.description: `mutation { toolName(arg: "value") }`: named arguments with GraphQL literal syntax.

url_call.name: HTTP request line
url_call.description: `POST /tool-name?arg=value`: a URL with a query string. Everything is a string, and nesting has to be flattened.

sexpr_call.name: S-expression call
sexpr_call.description: `(tool_name :arg "value" :count 3)`: Lisp-style keyword arguments with the least punctuation of any structured form.

json_object.name: JSON object call
json_object.description: Answer with {"name": ..., "arguments": {...}}. The default shape for almost every function-calling API.

json_array.name: JSON array of calls
json_array.description: Always answer with a JSON array, even for a single call. Removes the single-vs-parallel shape switch.

jsonl_call.name: One JSON call per line
jsonl_call.description: Each call on its own line as a complete JSON object. Makes parallel calls a line-oriented output rather than a nested one.

code_block_json.name: JSON inside a fenced code block
code_block_json.description: The call as JSON inside a ```json fence.

native.name: Provider-native tool API
native.description: Calls come back through the provider's own tool_calls field rather than as text.
native.real_world_origin: OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini native tool calling

nl_intent.name: Natural-language intent
nl_intent.description: The model says in words which tool it will use and with what values; a schema-guided rule adapter converts that to a call.

nl_intent_structured.name: Natural-language intent with a fixed sentence frame
nl_intent_structured.description: Natural language constrained to the frame 'Use TOOL with arg = value, arg = value.' Keeps the natural-language channel while removing most of the parsing ambiguity.

key_value_call.name: Key-value block
key_value_call.description: `TOOL: name` then one `arg: value` line each. Structured but with no brackets or quoting to get wrong.

yaml_call.name: YAML call block
yaml_call.description: The call as a small YAML document with name and arguments keys.

toml_call.name: TOML call block
toml_call.description: `[[call]]` array-of-tables with a name and an [call.arguments] table.

pipe_call.name: Pipe-delimited call (novel)
pipe_call.description: `tool|arg=value|arg=value` on one line. No brackets, no quotes, no indentation: a one-line call that still names its arguments.

csv_call.name: Positional CSV call (novel)
csv_call.description: `tool_name,value1,value2` with values in the schema's declared order, so the arguments are bound by position, not by name.

table_call.name: Markdown table call (novel)
table_call.description: One row per argument in a fixed three-column table. The grid makes a missing or invented argument visible to the model as it writes.

symbolic_call.name: Type-marked symbolic call (novel)
symbolic_call.description: `tool ★arg§value` where the symbol before each value restates its type. Pairs with the symbolic schema format so the type channel is consistent in both directions.

slot_fill_call.name: Template completion (novel)
slot_fill_call.description: The model is given the exact JSON skeleton and told to replace only the placeholder values.

two_step_call.name: Name first, then arguments (novel)
two_step_call.description: The model writes the tool name on its own line, then the arguments as JSON on the next. Splits selection from binding so the two failure modes can be attributed separately.

tool_call_tags.name: <tool_call> JSON tags
tool_call_tags.description: A JSON call inside <tool_call></tool_call>, the convention of the Hermes, Qwen and Granite templates.

function_tags.name: <function=…> tags
function_tags.description: A call as <function=NAME> with a JSON body or <parameter=K>V</parameter> children.

xml_call.name: <function_calls><invoke> XML
xml_call.description: Anthropic's prompt-level XML calling: an <invoke> element per call with one <parameter> element per argument. Values are text, so types have to be recovered from the schema.

xml_generic_call.name: <call><tool>..</tool><args>..</args></call>
xml_generic_call.description: A simpler XML shape where arguments are child elements named after the parameter. Fewer attributes to get right.

python_tag.name: <|python_tag|> call
python_tag.description: Llama 3.x's control-token convention: a Python-style call after a <|python_tag|> marker, terminated by <|eom_id|>.

react.name: Thought / Action / Action Input
react.description: The ReAct convention. The tool name and the arguments live on separate lines, which removes any need for nesting.

bracket_call.name: Inline [tool(args)] notation
bracket_call.description: Toolformer's inline notation: the call is embedded in the sentence between square brackets.
